body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Change | [Age](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Confidence](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) |
|---|---|---|---|
| [semgrep](https://redirect.github.com/semgrep/semgrep) ([changelog](https://redirect.github.com/semgrep/semgrep/blob/develop/CHANGELOG.md)) | `1.182.1` → `1.183.0` | ![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/pypi/semgrep/1.183.0?slim=true) | ![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/pypi/semgrep/1.182.1/1.183.0?slim=true) |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>semgrep/semgrep (semgrep)</summary>

### [`v1.183.0`](https://redirect.github.com/semgrep/semgrep/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#11830---2026-10-29)

##### ### Added

- The `--help` output of `semgrep` subcommands now includes a "THIRD-PARTY
  LICENSES" section linking to the licenses and notices for Semgrep's open
  source dependencies at <https://semgrep.dev/cli-credits>. (cli-credits)
- Pro: Supply Chain now records which Go module requires which when dependency paths are enabled and local builds are allowed, so transitive Go findings can show the dependency path. (SC-4268)

##### ### Changed

- Semgrep no longer ships binaries for Intel Macs; 1.182 is the last release that supports them. On Intel Macs, use the `semgrep/semgrep` Docker image; on Apple Silicon, use a native arm64 Python. (drop-intel-macos)
- Speed up scans with many rules that share file prefilter conditions by checking each condition once per file. (prefilter-predicate-memo)
- semgrep ci `--no-suppress-errors` now exits with code 2 (instead of 0) when dependency resolution fails for a subproject while local builds are allowed (--allow-local-builds): a build or package manager command fails, a lockfile cannot be parsed at all, or a build succeeds but reports an incomplete dependency list (for example, a registry refused a request). The affected dependency sources are listed in the scan output and the scan no longer reports that it completed successfully. Findings from the other subprojects are still reported. The default behavior, where errors are suppressed, is unchanged, and so is any scan without --allow-local-builds. Semgrep Managed Scanning scans are not affected. (SC-3613)
- bash grammar update (v0.25.1):

  - Bash arithmetic (`$(( ))`, `$[ ]`, `(( ))`, C-style `for` headers) is now translated into operator trees with bash precedence, so patterns such as `$(( $X * 2 ))` match structurally. `$((...))` is no longer confused with `$(...)`.
  - Bash patterns accept a lone `...` before `done`, `fi` or `}`, e.g. `while ...; do ... done`, and `until` loops now parse as loops.
  - Bash words containing `#` (`x=foo#bar`) are no longer truncated, and arguments after a redirect or heredoc delimiter stay with their command.
  - Many Bash constructs that failed to parse now parse, e.g. `$[ ]`, `time ( ... )`, extglob in `case` and `[[ ]]`, and `if` function bodies.

  (bash-v0.25.1)
- clojure grammar update (v0.0.13):

  - Clojure source parsing now accepts reader-evaluated metadata, such as ^#=(keyword "a") \[1 2], including the legacy #^ prefix. Semgrep does not execute reader evaluation, and metadata remains ignored during matching.
  - Clojure source parsing now supports reader conditionals inside symbolic values, such as ## #?(:clj Inf :cljs NaN), retaining the conditional branches without evaluating them.

  (clojure-v0.0.13)
- swift grammar update (0.5.0):

  - Swift parsing now supports type and value parameter packs, including each/repeat expansions and pack constraints.
  - Swift parsing now supports if and switch expressions used as variable initializers.
  - Swift parsing now supports macro declarations with typed signatures and #externalMacro definitions. This does not implement macro expansion.
  - Swift property observers now retain their willSet/didSet bodies and parameters separately from property initializers.
  - Swift parsing now supports borrowing, consuming, package, and distributed modifiers while preserving their distinct spellings.
  - Swift parsing now supports #unavailable conditions and distinguishes them from #available conditions. Both are mapped as `#…` expression nodes (not boolean `Not`) so patterns like `if !$X` do not match availability checks.
  - Swift parsing now supports member access on parenthesized existential types, such as (any P).self, and preserves the underlying parenthesized existential or opaque type.
  - Swift parsing now supports references to the bitwise AND operator using (&).

  (swift-0.5.0)

##### ### Fixed

- The Cursor hooks installed by `semgrep mcp` now track edited files separately for each Cursor conversation, so one window's stop scan no longer scans or discards another conversation's edits. (mcp-hook-cache-per-conversation)
- The `semgrep mcp` server's `semgrep_scan` tool now only scans files inside the client's workspace root, or the server's working directory when the client reports none. Set `SEMGREP_MCP_ALLOW_SCAN_OUTSIDE_WORKSPACE=true` to scan files outside it. (mcp-scan-workspace-roots)
- Interfile scans no longer fail with `Failure: Failed to unmarshal cached
  value: Exception during parallelization: Exception.Timeout(...)` when a
  taint configuration timeout fires at an unlucky moment. The timeout now only
  skips the affected rule and file, as intended. (CODE-9810)
- The Semgrep source distribution on PyPI is once again published with provenance. (CODE-10070)
- Update certificate trust in Semgrep and its container images to address the eMudhra certificate authority compromise. Disable curl-based telemetry on macOS and Windows; default telemetry and scanning remain available. (INCID-521)
- Supply Chain: multi-document pnpm-lock.yaml files (written by pnpm 11+) are
  now parsed instead of reporting zero dependencies. A lockfile that fails to
  parse now marks its subproject as unresolved rather than resolved with zero
  dependencies. (SC-3870)
- Supply Chain now parses go.mod files that contain a `godebug ( ... )` block. Such files used to report no dependencies and a parse error. (SC-4268)
- Supply Chain now finds the direct dependencies of Poetry projects that declare them in the `[project] dependencies` table (Poetry 2.0 and later), in dependency groups or as extras, instead of reporting every package with unknown transitivity. Packages from Poetry dependency groups are now reported as direct. PyPI rule matching now ignores differences in case, `-`, `_` and `.` in package names, so rules match however a lockfile spells the name. (SC-4278)
- Supply Chain now parses yarn.lock files generated by yarn 0.16 and earlier, whose header has no blank line after `# yarn lockfile v1`. Previously these failed with "Failed to parse yarn.lock at 1:1" and no dependencies were analyzed. (SC-4286)
- Recognize all valid Python f-string prefixes without accepting invalid prefix combinations. ([gh-11913](https://redirect.github.com/semgrep/semgrep/issues/11913))

##### ### Infra/Release Changes

- Apply external rule-test expectations consistently in CLI and OCaml CI tests. (rule-expectation-ci)
- Add --override-expectations to the OCaml rule test runner to replace expected finding lines for individual targets, rules, and engines from an external JSON file. (rule-test-expectations)

- Semgrep no longer logs credentials embedded in a proxy URL (for example
  `HTTPS_PROXY=http://user:password@proxy:8080`) when it reports the configured
  proxy settings. (proxy-log-redact-userinfo)
- Logs and traces no longer include snippets of the scanned source code when a
  file fails to parse. Parsing exceptions now report the file, line, column, and
  the length of the unexpected text instead. Dependency resolution errors for
  malformed lockfiles are reported the same way. (redact-source-in-telemetry)
- pro: Reduced peak memory for large projects (CODE-10136)
- Supply Chain: the yarn v1 lockfile parser no longer reports a package named
  "dependencies" with an empty version when a blank line precedes the
  dependencies block of an entry, and it now keeps that entry's dependency
  edges. Entries without a version line are reported as parser errors instead
  of dependencies with an empty version. (SC-4214)
- Gradle module attribution now works for modules whose logical project name
  does not match their directory (a renamed `include` or a remapped
  `projectDir` in settings.gradle). The resolver's init script reports each
  project's actual build file, and dependencies are attributed to that file
  instead of falling back to the root manifest. (SC-4327)
- semgrep ci --no-suppress-errors with --allow-local-builds: when dependency resolution fails and the scan exits with code 2, the reason is now also in the `errors` of the JSON output (one entry per resolver error or lockfile parse error of each failed subproject, or a generic entry if none was reported; resolver errors include the failed command and the end of its output, with common credential shapes such as URL credentials and Authorization headers redacted), not only in the log. Previously the JSON had no error, so pipelines that read it could not tell why the scan failed. (SC-4348)

title: GH#67: give each third-party image its own code-scanning category
body:
## Summary

Each third-party image gets its own code-scanning category, `images/<repository>/`, so a scan of one image closes only that image's alerts. A failed image scan after its retry leaves that image's category out of the written SARIF instead of the whole `images/` set, so the other images' alerts stay current, and a pin-scoped run writes runs for the images it scanned alone. The new `-upload-dir` writes the upload set as a directory of SARIF files of at most 20 runs, because a file per image exceeds code scanning's per-file cap; `--out` still writes one file for `accept`, the artifact and the baseline recipe. `accept` keeps an image entry when the input holds no run for that image's category. README documents the per-image categories, the directory upload, and the manual deletion an image that stops being pinned needs.

## Files Changed

README.md, cmd/scanctl/accept.go, cmd/scanctl/accept_test.go, cmd/scanctl/main.go, internal/dismiss/dismiss_test.go, internal/report/report.go, internal/report/report_test.go, internal/runner/image.go, internal/runner/image_test.go, internal/runner/runner.go, internal/sarif/sarif.go, internal/sarif/sarif_test.go

The workflow change below rides in this body: this worker's token has no `workflow` scope, so it cannot push `.github/**`.

## Decisions

One category per image rather than leaving the whole `images/` category out: the issue's fourth acceptance bullet requires a scheduled run with one failed image scan to keep the other images' alerts current. An image that stops being pinned keeps its alerts until its code-scanning configuration is deleted by hand, as README documents; closing it from scanctl would need the GitHub API.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** self-assessed, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `go test -count=1 ./...` pass (cmd/scanctl 7.4s, every package ok). New tests cover one code-scanning category per image, a failed image scan leaving only its own category out, the upload set carrying every image and clearing earlier files, and `accept` keeping an entry whose image category the input lacks.

## Reserved files

`.github/workflows/github-reusable.yml`, three hunks:

```diff
-          "$(go env GOPATH)/bin/scanctl" run $gate_flag $profile_flag $baseline_flag $dismiss_flag $import_flag $own_flag \
-            --out scanctl.sarif --sbom sbom.cdx.json \
+          "$(go env GOPATH)/bin/scanctl" run $gate_flag $profile_flag $baseline_flag $dismiss_flag $import_flag $own_flag \
+            --out scanctl.sarif --upload-dir scanctl-sarif --sbom sbom.cdx.json \
             --summary scanctl-summary.md "$SCAN_PATH"
```

```diff
       - name: Upload SARIF to code scanning
         if: always() && github.event.repository.private != true
         uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@87557b9c84dde89fdd9b10e88954ac2f4248e463 # v4
         with:
-          sarif_file: scanctl.sarif
-        continue-on-error: true
+          sarif_file: scanctl-sarif
```

```diff
         uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7
         with:
           name: scanctl-results
           path: |
-            scanctl.sarif
+            scanctl-sarif
             sbom.cdx.json
           if-no-files-found: ignore
```

`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, three hunks:

```diff
       - name: Run scanctl on itself
-        run: ./scanctl run --out scanctl.sarif --summary "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" .
+        run: ./scanctl run --out scanctl.sarif --upload-dir upload-sarif --summary "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" .
```

```diff
       - name: Upload SARIF to code scanning
         if: always()
         uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@87557b9c84dde89fdd9b10e88954ac2f4248e463 # v4
         with:
-          sarif_file: scanctl.sarif
-        continue-on-error: true
+          sarif_file: upload-sarif
```

```diff
         uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7
         with:
           name: scanctl-sarif
-          path: scanctl.sarif
+          path: upload-sarif
           if-no-files-found: ignore
```

Dropping `continue-on-error` is the second half of the issue: a rejected upload now fails the job instead of leaving the previous alerts green. The upload set holds the same runs the single file held, so the artifact keeps the findings a private repo cannot upload.

## Scenarios checked

none: no ops bench scenario, scenario helper or app `test.yml` asserts scanctl's SARIF categories or its upload shape.

## Bench to prove it

none: no behaviour the bench asserts.

## Findings

- https://github.com/catenahq/scanctl/issues/79: delete the code-scanning category of an image that stops being pinned. This change documents the manual deletion; automating it needs the code-scanning analyses API.

Resolves #67

### [`v1.185.0`](https://redirect.github.com/semgrep/semgrep/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#11850---2026-11-10)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/semgrep/semgrep/compare/v1.184.0...v1.185.0)

##### ### Added

- Secrets: emit structured, privacy-safe telemetry for custom validator HTTP requests (hostname, port, status, latency, rule/scan correlation) (SMS-3122)

##### ### Changed

- The `semgrep/semgrep` Docker image no longer includes the OpenSSH server (`sshd`) or `sftp-server`. It now installs only the OpenSSH client (`ssh`, `scp`, `ssh-keyscan`, `ssh-agent`, `ssh-add` and `ssh-keygen`), which is all git needs to fetch over SSH. Container scanners will no longer report sshd-only CVEs against the image. (docker-ssh-client-only)
- julia grammar update (v0.25.0):

  - Julia source parsing and rule patterns now support public API declarations while distinguishing them from export declarations and calls named public.
  - Julia source parsing and rule patterns now support outer-qualified loop bindings, preserving their distinction from ordinary bindings and a variable named outer.
  - Julia parsing and matching now support typed const fields without initializers in mutable structs.
  - Julia source parsing and rule patterns now support renaming imported macros, such as import A: [@​m](https://redirect.github.com/m) as [@​n](https://redirect.github.com/n) and import A: [@​m](https://redirect.github.com/m) as [@​B](https://redirect.github.com/B).n, and keep the @​ on macro names in imports, exports, and public declarations.
  - Julia rules can now match unary ± expressions and distinguish binary ± from ∓, reducing operator-related false positives.
  - Julia numeral juxtaposition such as 1__2 is now represented as multiplication by \_\_2 and can be found by multiplication patterns.
  - Julia function-definition patterns now retain where constraints, avoiding matches against definitions with a different constraint.

  (julia-v0.25.0)

##### ### Fixed

- OCaml: taint analysis now follows data through expression statements and
  sequence expressions. For example, in `let x = (r := 1; source ()) in sink x`,
  the value of the sequence is the result of `source ()`, so the finding on
  `sink x` is now reported. Taint also no longer leaks from one `match` case
  into the next one. (ocaml-expression-statements)
- OCaml: the last expression of a function body is now treated as the function's result, so taint flows through calls. (ocaml-implicit-returns)
- On Windows, Semgrep now runs programs it calls by name, such as git and pysemgrep, only from fully qualified PATH directories. Previously Windows checked the current directory first, so an executable committed to a scanned repository could run during a scan. Initially reported by Aikido Security. (CODE-10122)
